user.title: Add a device by address
user.description: Devices are normally found automatically. Use this only if Home Assistant cannot see the device on the network (for example it is on another VLAN).

data_description.host: The address of the device, for example 192.168.1.20.
data_description.port: The port the Piston plugin listens on (47830 unless you changed it).

confirm.title: Decky device found
confirm.description: Found {name}. Next, enter the code shown on the device to pair it with Home Assistant.

pair.title: Pair {name}
pair.description: Open the Piston panel on the device and enter the code shown there.

data_description.code: The six digits shown in the plugin panel on the device. The code is valid for five minutes.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: The device no longer accepts this Home Assistant. In the plugin panel choose Reset pairing, then continue and enter the new code.

reconfigure.title: Change the address of {name}
reconfigure.description: Use this when the device has a new address and Home Assistant does not find it by itself. The pairing is kept.

data_description.host: The new address of the device, for example 192.168.1.20.
data_description.port: The port the Piston plugin listens on (47830 unless you changed it).

error.wrong_code: That code is not right. Check the code on the device and try again.
error.code_expired: The code expired. A new code is now shown on the device.
error.code_locked: Too many wrong codes. Wait a minute, then enter the new code shown on the device.
error.version_skew: The plugin and the integration versions are not compatible. Update the one that is older.
error.already_paired: The device is already paired. In the plugin panel choose Reset pairing first.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the device. Check that it is on and on the same network.

abort.already_configured: This device is already set up.
abort.already_paired: The device is already paired with another Home Assistant. In the plugin panel choose Reset pairing, then try again.
abort.not_supported: This device did not identify itself and cannot be set up.
abort.wrong_device: A different device answered. Try again.

data_description.turn_off: Sleep (suspend) can be woken again with Wake on LAN. Shutdown needs the power button on most devices.
data_description.pip_cameras: Cameras offered in the PiP camera selector. The show_pip action works with any camera.
data_description.sensor_interval: How often the device reports temperatures, load and battery. Shorter updates more often but uses a little more power.
data_description.pip_position: Where the camera picture appears on the device screen by default.
data_description.pip_size: How large the camera picture is by default.
data_description.pip_duration: How long the camera picture stays before it hides itself by default. The show_pip action can override this.
data_description.pip_mute: Start camera pictures without sound by default.
data_description.allow_all_users: The remote card moves the pointer and types on the device. By default only administrators can use it; turn this on to let every user.

version_skew_old.title: The plugin on {name} is too old
version_skew_old.description: Update the Piston plugin on the device (in Decky Loader) so it matches this integration. Plugins from version 0.4.0 on are updated by Home Assistant itself.

version_skew_new.title: The Piston integration is too old for {name}
version_skew_new.description: Update the integration in HACS, then restart Home Assistant.

device_unreachable.title: {name} has not been reachable for over a day
device_unreachable.description: Home Assistant could not connect to {name} for more than 24 hours. If the device is normally switched off, you can ignore this; the message disappears when it connects again. Otherwise check that it is on, that the Piston plugin is running on it and that it is on the same network.

plugin_update_failed.title: The plugin update on {name} failed
plugin_update_failed.description: Home Assistant asked {name} to install plugin version {version}, but {reason}. The old plugin is still installed and Home Assistant will not try again by itself. Press Install on the Plugin update entity to retry, or install the plugin zip from the GitHub release through Decky Loader.

version_skew_updatable.title: The plugin on {name} does not match this integration
version_skew_updatable.description: The plugin on {name} is a different version from this integration and automatic plugin updates are off. Press Install on the Plugin update entity, or turn on Install plugin updates automatically.

plugin_update_confirm.title: Approve the plugin update on {name}
plugin_update_confirm.description: Home Assistant has an update ready for the Piston plugin on {name}. Decky Loader asks for your approval on the device: open the Decky Loader dialog ("Install Piston") and tap OK. If the device is in desktop mode, switch it to game mode first. If the dialog was dismissed, press Install on the Plugin update entity to ask again.

show_toast.name: Show toast
show_toast.description: Show a notification on the device.

title.name: Title
title.description: Heading of the toast. Defaults to Home Assistant.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the toast stays, in seconds.

silent.name: Silent
silent.description: Do not play the notification sound.

id.name: ID
id.description: Passed back in the click event so automations can tell toasts apart.

show_pip.name: Show PiP
show_pip.description: Show a camera over whatever is on the device. Replaces any camera already showing.

position.name: Position
position.description: Where on the screen. Defaults to the integration option.

duration.name: Hide after
duration.description: Seconds before it hides; Until hidden keeps it. Defaults to the integration option.
